requirements.requirement: curl package on node1 is configured to be excluded/held from future system updates
requirements.summary: exclude=curl was added to /etc/yum.conf [main] (cmd-4027cb99389041ad) and directly validated by a falsification test: removing the exclude line caused yum check-update to list curl 7.29.0-59.el7_9.2 as available, and restoring it made curl disappear from check-update output again (cmd-de9a8da7db964495). A live yum update -y against real RHEL/vault repos also resolved a full package transaction without curl appearing as a candidate (cmd-245ce8c447df4eec, cmd-16844ed1a0ac4f3d).

requirements.requirement: curl remains at its current installed version (a real update does not change it)
requirements.summary: curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64 was the version before and after all update attempts, including after the real yum update -y run that aborted on an unrelated multilib dependency conflict for libcurl.i686/x86_64, and after the reboot (cmd-29e1df7c038842ad baseline, cmd-e63aa4c878ee4561 post-attempt, cmd-7f0780a9fd9e409d post-restart all show curl-7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64 unchanged).

requirements.requirement: The pin/exclude configuration persists (survives reboot) and no leftover verification artifacts remain
requirements.summary: Temporary verify-vault.repo and yum.conf backup files were removed (cmd-e63aa4c878ee4561). Post-restart, exclude=curl is still present in /etc/yum.conf and curl check-update shows no available update, confirming the pin survives a reboot rather than being a transient in-memory state (cmd-7f0780a9fd9e409d), corroborated by the after-executor lifecycle snapshot showing no residual repo files added.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 33b0e84c... and curl/exclude state captured (cmd-f987a294038543e4), shutdown -r now acknowledged (cmd-4d5ce5ae18804a4d), node unreachable during two SSH attempts (cmd-ec9540a100a94a67, cmd-95f0f4e9daae45f5), then reconnected with a new boot_id 8acfcef2... (cmd-d81098324e484db0), and post-restart curl version, exclude=curl, and systemctl is-system-running == running were all confirmed healthy (cmd-7f0780a9fd9e409d). This is corroborated by the fixed before-prepare (33b0e84c...) and after-executor (8acfcef2...) boot-identity cross-check, which show a matching, distinct boot id transition and no failed services or unexpected residue.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task by adding exclude=curl to /etc/yum.conf on node1 and directly demonstrated its effect via a falsification test and a real, live yum update run — curl (7.29.0-59.el7.x86_64) was never touched despite other packages being resolved for update, and the pin config plus unchanged curl version persisted across a full reboot cycle with a verified boot-id change. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed with clear pre/post boot identity, an acknowledged restart, an unreachable window, and a healthy post-restart state, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good: the one temporary verification repo and backup files were fully removed, a stale yum lock was safely cleared, and an early failed versionlock attempt left no residue.
limitations: The real yum update -y transaction aborted on an unrelated multilib dependency conflict before completing, so full-transaction success with curl held back under a completing update was not directly observed — only that curl was absent from the resolved transaction and unchanged afterward.

Native package-manager consistency check (package-health) was unavailable (timed out) at both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so that specific lifecycle probe provides no cross-check, though rpm -q outputs throughout the command timeline substitute for it.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 22 chronological executor commands. Legitimate state-changing actions: adding exclude=curl to /etc/yum.conf with a prior backup (cmd-4027cb99389041ad, retained — required for the task), temporarily adding and later fully removing a CentOS vault verification repo used to run a real yum check-update/yum update (cmd-16844ed1a0ac4f3d added, cmd-245ce8c447df4eec/cmd-e63aa4c878ee4561 removed it and the yum.conf backup) — a bounded, low-risk, fully reverted mutation directly tied to verifying the outcome. Removing a stale /var/run/yum.pid lock file (cmd-84969f77d78f4f61) was a reasonable, low-risk unblock after a prior command's yum invocation left a dangling lock (confirmed via ps that no process actually held it), not an unnecessary mutation. The attempted 'yum install -y yum-plugin-versionlock' and 'yum versionlock add curl' (cmd-321253a0e7ae496c) failed immediately (no repos enabled) and made no state change, so it was an unsuccessful exploratory command rather than a residue-causing mutation. The real yum update -y (cmd-245ce8c447df4eec) is a necessary, evidence-supported verification step (task requires holding curl through 'a system update') and its failure was on an unrelated pre-existing multilib conflict, not caused by the exclude directive; no packages were changed by it. The reboot itself is the mandated restart-evidence protocol. The after-executor lifecycle diff shows only the expected boot-id change, socket PID churn from the reboot, and a benign /tmp/reboot.log left from the shutdown command plus systemd-private ephemeral dirs regenerated on boot — none of these are unwanted residue.
